title: docs(adr-0135): a cloud-managed environment keeps the roster and authorization; credentials stay in the cloud
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-support-ai"} -->
_Requested by **Yibo Wang** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01BVUyyPie8gHwoPM18iABwB?thread=cmsg_01BVUyyPie8gHwoPM18iABwBFbmjyQW99NhGPQG4JPyTSz)_
Fixes #33184

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- **改了什么**：ADR-0135 的 D5.2 下新增一条注记（+61 行，只增不改）：托管环境（`OS_CLOUD_MANAGED=1`）上，账号凭据归云端，名册和授权归环境。环境管理员在「设置 → 用户」里添加、导入、停用人员，由环境请云端发邀请；组织所有者/管理员在环境里持有 `admin_full_access`，这是唯一从云端投射下来的授权；自托管不变。
- **为什么改**：云端 ADR-0024 已在 2026-11-14 按 cloud#4465 的裁决 7、9、10 修订（cloud PR #4474），本仓的 ADR-0135 是它的公开镜像，此前只同步了「托管没有应急本地管理员」这一半（PR #33248）。席位和 agent 按 ADR 做设计，缺这条规则会做出与托管身份相冲突的设计。
- **风险与回滚**：只改一份 ADR 文本，不动代码、schema 和生成产物，不发布任何包；决定仍以云端记录为准，本注记与云端不一致时算本注记的错。回滚即还原本 PR。
- **先看**：`docs/adr/0135-identity-and-access-architecture.md` 新注记里的「One authorization is projected from the cloud」一段（唯一的 D5 例外，写入方标为 cloud-side），其次第一段和四条要点（与云端原文的逐句对照表见下）。
- **两分钟验证**：`pnpm check:adr-symbol-anchors`，预期退出 0 并报「3717 anchors across 157 records resolve」，比 main（`9e6fee19`）的 3704 多 13，即本注记的 13 个代码锚点全部解析。
- **需要你做的**：受管路径（`docs/adr/**`）：请审阅这条注记并合并本 PR。

## What changes

One file, `docs/adr/0135-identity-and-access-architecture.md` (+61 / −0): one dated note under D5.2, placed after the 2026-11-14 break-glass note and in the same house style. It mirrors the 2026-11-14 amendment of cloud ADR-0024 at this record's granularity. No D-body is rewritten and no clause is added.

Provenance, as triage comment 6895807038 gives it and as the note's header carries it: cloud ADR-0024, amended 2026-11-14, cloud#4465 rulings 7, 9 and 10, cloud PR #4474 @ 312f2e5e. The source text is the director's verbatim copy on the card (comment 6912778378; `objectstack-ai/cloud` `docs/adr/0024-identity-and-access-architecture.md`, merge commit `312f2e5efc83c73d2bc5fec5bed62e099d00e6f5`). This session cannot read `objectstack-ai/cloud`, so the card's copy binds.

### Source to mirror

Left: the cloud sentence, verbatim from comment 6912778378. Right: the sentence of the new note that carries it.

| Cloud ADR-0024, 2026-11-14 amendment | ADR-0135, the new note |
|---|---|
| **hosted: credentials live in the cloud; the roster and authorization live in the environment.** | Title: "on a cloud-managed environment, credentials live in the cloud; the roster and authorization live in the environment." |
| Every person remains their own cloud account, and D5.1 is unchanged: the OP issues a code only to a `sys_member` of the environment's organization. | "Every person on a hosted environment (`OS_CLOUD_MANAGED=1`) remains their own cloud account and signs in through the hosting cloud's identity provider, and the cloud's own sign-in gate (`cloud ADR-0024 D5.1`, which stays in the cloud record) is unchanged." D5.1's own rule is not restated: it is on this record's "What stays in `cloud` ADR-0024" list. |
| What moves is who starts the lifecycle. An environment administrator adds, imports and deactivates people in Setup → Users. | "What moves is who starts a person's lifecycle: an environment administrator adds, imports and deactivates people in Setup → Users." The bullets "Add and import" and "Deactivate" then name this repository's doors (second table). |
| The environment asks the control plane to invite the address as `member`. | Bullet "The environment asks; the cloud invites": "The environment sends no invitation of its own. It reaches its host through one seam … By the cloud record, the control plane invites the address as `member` …" |
| Deactivating a plain member ends that membership; an owner or admin is changed in the console only. | "… and deactivating a plain member ends that membership." and the bullet "An owner or admin is changed in the console only." |
| The request ends in better-auth's own `sys_invitation` / `sys_member` writes and passes every gate a console invitation passes (D9: no second invitation store, no cloud-side roster). | "… through better-auth's own `sys_invitation` and `sys_member` writes and every gate a console invitation passes (no second invitation store and no cloud-side roster, D9) …" |
| For hosted, D5.2's `idp-provisioned` column reads: Admin add-user and Deactivate **in the environment**; Invite **sent by the cloud on the environment's request**; Password management still **none**. | "For hosted, the managed side of D5.2's surface therefore reads: add and deactivate in the environment, the invitation sent by the cloud on the environment's request, and password management still none." This record carries no D5.2 table, so the cloud's column is named as the managed side of the surface. |
| Unchanged: D1, self-hosted deployments, the console's own invitation. | "Unchanged: D1, self-hosted deployments (off a managed environment the two add doors answer `409`, and the local doors hold as D5.2 states them) and the cloud console's own invitation." |
| One authorization is projected from the cloud: an organization owner or admin holds `admin_full_access` in the environment while that role lasts (ruling 9). | "**One authorization is projected from the cloud, and it is the only exception to D5**: an organization owner or admin holds `admin_full_access` in the environment while that role lasts (ruling 9)." |
| This is the only exception to D5; every other position and permission set is assigned in the environment, and nothing is projected upward. | "Every other position and permission set is assigned in the environment, and nothing is projected upward, from the environment to the cloud." |
| Hosted has no local break-glass admin; emergency access is a platform-operator procedure, and self-hosted deployments keep local admins (ruling 10). (And the correction under the D5.2 invariant.) | "The same amendment's ruling 10, no local break-glass administrator on a hosted environment, is the note above and is not restated here." That note landed with PR #33248. |
| **SCIM:** cloud#500's cloud-to-environment fan-out is not needed under this model (D6: per production environment, not fan-out); if hosted ever offers bring-your-own IdP with SCIM, the customer's IdP provisions straight into the environment roster through the framework's SCIM path. Whether such a person also holds a cloud membership is decided with that offer. | "The amendment also finds the cloud-to-environment SCIM fan-out not needed: if hosted ever offers a bring-your-own identity provider with SCIM, that provider provisions straight into the environment's roster through this repository's SCIM path (D6), and whether such a person also holds a cloud membership is decided with that offer." |
| **Supersedes (only these; everything else in cloud#3132 stands):** … D4's `idp-provisioned` row, where identity is not editable in the environment, as far as the roster lifecycle goes (the environment now adds, imports and deactivates the person; credentials stay in the cloud) … | "… as far as the roster lifecycle goes: D2 reads a managed person's row as a mirror of the directory that owns it, and on a hosted environment the environment itself adds, imports and deactivates that person while the credential stays the cloud's. What the amendment supersedes in the cloud's own text and console copy is listed in the cloud record and stays there." The rest of the list (two cloud rulings, the console copy, the columns of the cloud's own D5.2 table) names cloud text this record does not carry. |
| The D1–D10 bodies are not rewritten; for hosted deployments this note governs where they disagree. | "The D-bodies are not rewritten. For a hosted environment this note governs where they disagree …" and "The cloud record is the decision: a difference between it and this note is this note's bug." |

Not mirrored, because it is the cloud record's own bookkeeping or its commercial half: the "(refines the 2026-10-21 amendment, does not reverse it)" relation and the inline edits to that amendment, the Phasing and Subsumes lines, the cloud#500 status corrections, and the tiering table and paragraph.

### Framework facts the note states, and the code at `9e6fee19` behind each

| Sentence in the note | Code at the base |
|---|---|
| Setup → Users offers a platform administrator two actions, on a managed environment only. | `packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-user.object.ts`, actions `add_sso_user` and `import_sso_users`: `visible` is the platform-admin standing and `features.cloudManaged`. |
| Their doors add the person as a pending row: `sys_user.source` reads `idp_pending`, with no password and no account link, and with the positions, permission sets and manager the administrator chose. The first sign-in through the hosting cloud's identity provider binds to that row. | `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/pending-sso-users.ts` (`runAddSsoUser`, `runImportSsoUsers`, and the module header), `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/pending-sso-marker.ts` (`PENDING_SSO_SOURCE`). |
| `admin/ban-user` and `admin/unban-user` deactivate and reactivate a person, and `admin/remove-sso-user` removes one who is still pending. | `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/admin-ban-endpoints.ts` (`runAdminBanUser`, `runAdminUnbanUser`), `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/pending-sso-users.ts` (`runRemoveSsoUser`). |
| The environment reaches its host through one seam; the host is told after a person is added, and asked before a person is deactivated, reactivated or removed. | `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/environment-user-host.ts` (`EnvironmentUserHost`), wired as the `environmentUserHost` option in `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-plugin.ts`. |
| What the host does with the call is cloud-side, not in this repo. | `git grep -n environmentUserHost` outside `packages/plugins/plugin-auth`: 4 hits, all prose (the authentication guide, the QA checklist, one CHANGELOG twice), none in source. Control: 4 hits in `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src` outside tests. |
| The seam carries a typed refusal for an owner or admin: the host answers `409` and the row stays as it was, and a deactivation whose host call fails is refused too. | `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/environment-user-host.ts` (`EnvironmentUserHostRefusal`, and the module header: a deactivation asks the host before its write; any other host failure answers `503` and writes nothing). |
| The environment's own doors that invite a member, remove one or change a member's role answer `409` on a managed environment. | `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/cloud-managed.ts` (`CLOUD_MANAGED_REFUSAL_MESSAGES`: `invitation`, `removeMember`, `updateMemberRole`). |
| What gives and withdraws the projected `admin_full_access` as the cloud role changes is cloud-side, not in this repo, and D5's derivation is not changed for it. | Read at `9e6fee19`: no source in this tree keys an `admin_full_access` grant on a cloud organization role. The writers that come closest do something else: `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/auto-org-admin-grant.ts` grants `organization_admin` from this environment's own `sys_member` grade and never `admin_full_access`; the identity-provider group projection (`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/scim-group-projection.ts`, `sso-group-projection.ts`) grants ordinary sets only (its header: "an identity provider's group never confers administrator standing"); `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/bootstrap-platform-admin.ts` promotes the first user that can sign in, or reports the configured owners, and reads no cloud role. The other grant inserts a grep for the grant table finds under `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src` (`admin-user-endpoints.ts`, `pending-sso-users.ts`, `auth-manager-membership-admission.ts`, `demo-staff.ts`) write the set an administrator, the self-registration setting or the demo seed names. The derivation is `packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.ts` (`hasPlatformAdminStanding`). This is a reading of those files, not a census of every caller of the data API. |
| Off a managed environment the two add doors answer `409`. | `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/pending-sso-marker.ts` (`PENDING_SSO_MESSAGES.notManaged`, `PENDING_SSO_REFUSAL_STATUS`). |

## Why

Triage 6920260070: this records a design rule, not wording. Seats and agents design from the ADRs, and without this note ADR-0135 reads as though a managed person's place on the roster can only be started and ended outside the environment, and as though no authorization ever comes from the cloud. The code for the environment half is already on `main` (the pending-person doors and the host seam, PR #33227 and PR #34162; the Setup → Users actions, PR #33755; the membership doors a managed environment refuses, PR #34281), and the record did not say what it implements.

## Tests

n/a: docs only. No code, schema, test or generated artifact moves. No ablation: a document is not ablated.

## Acceptance notes

- **Date.** The note is dated 2026-11-16, the day this record gains it; the cloud amendment's own date, 2026-11-14, is in the provenance string. The existing notes carry the date they were written.
- **Placement.** Under D5.2, after the break-glass note, because the cloud amendment restates its own D5.2 surface and its correction sits under the D5.2 invariant. The note names D5 for the projected authorization and D2 for the mirror reading. It sits inside `## Decision`, so `addOnlyNoteReasons` in `scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs` reads the PR as Tier H (a line under a heading that names the decision), which is the landing the order names.
- **Two sentences beyond the order's list, both in the source.** The SCIM sentence and the "managed side of D5.2's surface" sentence are not in the order's "What to do" list. Both are sentences of the cloud amendment, and the SCIM one names this repository's SCIM path. The seat can cut either.
- **`idp_pending` and D2's "exactly two values".** D2's body says `sys_user.source` "carries exactly two values". Since PR #33227 the field has a third, `idp_pending`. The note records the third value where it describes the pending row; the D2 body is not rewritten (the order forbids it). Noted here, not filed.
- **Ruling 7.** The provenance string names rulings 7, 9 and 10. The cloud text attributes sentences to rulings 9 and 10 only, and cloud#4465 is not readable from here, so the note attributes no sentence to ruling 7.
- **Attribution link.** The second line of this body carries this card thread's link, as the session's attribution rule requires, not the seat thread's link the order prints. Reported as a deviation.
- **Assignee and reviewer.** `pr_create` carries the claim's `Account:` as the assignee (`.claude/agents/os-dev.md` rule 2). The order said no assignee; the agent file wins over an order, and the seat agreed before the PR opened. No reviewer is requested here: hand-over is the seat's.
- `skip-changeset` is declared on `pr_create`: `docs/adr/**` publishes nothing.
